approved: Social Services and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2013
Social Services and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2013 — In Committee — Keep schedule 1 (on gambling) unchanged
Social Services and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2013 - Third Reading - Read a third time

Outlined Labor's response to the Social Services and Other Legislation Amendment Bill, supporting continued Cape York welfare reform funding and changes to pension and family payment rules, but opposing new interest charges on student welfare debts, citing estimates that problem gambling costs Australia $5 billion a year on top of $19 billion in annual gambling losses.

Defended the government's Social Services and Other Legislation Amendment Bill, noting all but two of its measures originated under the previous Labor government, and cited estimates that problem gambling costs $5 billion a year against $19 billion in total gambling losses, while backing voluntary rather than mandatory poker machine precommitment.

Opposed parts of the Social Services and Other Legislation Amendment Bill, particularly interest charges on student debts and the childcare rebate freeze, while supporting continued Cape York Family Responsibility Commission funding, and said university funding rose from $8.1 billion in 2007 to $14 billion in 2013 under Labor with 190,000 more students enrolled.

Supported the Social Services and Other Legislation Amendment Bill, defending voluntary rather than mandatory poker machine precommitment by noting compulsive gambling nearly doubled after Norway introduced mandatory precommitment in 2009, and outlined the coalition's new paid parental leave scheme, from 1 July 2015, paying mothers 26 weeks at their actual wage.

Supported continued funding for the Cape York welfare reform trial in the Social Services and Other Legislation Amendment Bill, crediting Noel Pearson's leadership and reporting that two-thirds of surveyed residents felt the reforms had been positive while 52 per cent said people were trying to be better parents, and criticised the freeze on the childcare rebate cap.

Argued for the Social Services and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2013, which aims to cut $1 billion a year in red tape, extend the residency requirement for full pensions paid overseas from 25 to 35 years, and legislate $105.8 million in childcare savings that Labor banked but never enacted.

Opposed measures in the Social Services and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2013, defending Labor's economic record with debt at one-tenth the OECD average, and criticised the government for scrapping the $410 primary and $820 high school schoolkids bonus after promising before the election that no school would be worse off.

Supported continuing the Cape York Welfare Reform trial's income management scheme for a further two years at a cost of $4.2 million, citing Aurukun's school attendance rising from 46.1 per cent in 2008 to about 76 per cent under the Families Responsibilities Commission.

Opposed the Social Services and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2013 for repealing last year's gambling reforms including the national regulator and ATM withdrawal limits, citing Productivity Commission estimates that problem gambling costs $4.7 billion a year nationally, and criticised the bill's scrapping of student start-up loans for disadvantaged students.
Argued that the Social Services and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2013 would ease the administrative burden on small business, focusing his remarks on that provision.

Opposed provisions of the Social Services and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2013 that scrap the instant asset write-off, cutting the threshold from $6½ thousand back to $1,000 instead of Labor's planned rise to $10,000, and cited a welfare debt interest rate that has averaged 11.07 per cent over four years and currently stands at 9.6 per cent.

Opposed winding back the 43rd Parliament's poker machine reforms, citing Productivity Commission findings that 95,000 Australians with a gambling problem lose about $5,000 million a year, and noted the Australian Hotels Association and ClubsNSW donated $1.3 million to major parties after the 2010 election.

Opposing most provisions in the Social Services and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2013, the Greens criticised the government for rushing through 13 separate measures including university funding cuts, a freeze on the childcare rebate indexation, delaying the Charities Act 2013, extending income management in Cape York, and removing employer roles in paid parental leave; Labor supported some measures such as extending indexation pauses on higher family payment thresholds and closing the Pension Bonus Scheme but opposed the interest charge on student welfare debts, the childcare rebate freeze, and the last-minute postponement of the Charities Act definition.
